sanskrit: rāmas tasyāḥ priyaṃ kurvan dhanur ādāya satvaraḥ rakṣārthe lakṣmaṇaṃ nyasya prayayau mṛgalipsayā
english: Rāma, wishing to please her, quickly took up his bow, stationed Lakṣmaṇa to guard her, and went off in pursuit of the deer.

sanskrit: sa dhanvī baddhatūṇīraḥ khaḍgagodhāṅgulitravān anvadhāvan mṛgaṃ rāmo rudras tārāmṛgaḥ yathā
english: Bearing his bow, quiver fastened, sword at his side, leather wrist-guard on his fingers, Rāma chased the deer — as Rudra pursues the celestial deer among the stars.

sanskrit: so 'ntarhitaḥ punas tasya darśanaṃ rākṣaso vrajan cakarṣa mahad adhvānaṃ rāmas taṃ bubudhe tataḥ
english: The demon, going unseen, lured Rāma's gaze onward; it repeatedly vanished and reappeared, drawing him far along a great distance — and then Rāma understood what it was.

sanskrit: niśācaraṃ viditvā taṃ rāghavaḥ pratibhānavān amoghaṃ śaram ādāya jaghāna mṛgarūpiṇam
english: Recognizing it as a night-roaming demon, the quick-witted son of Raghu fitted an unerring arrow to his bow and slew the creature that had taken the form of a deer.

sanskrit: sa rāmabāṇābhihataḥ kṛtvā rāmasvaraṃ tadā hā sīte lakṣmaṇety evaṃ cukrośārtasvareṇa ha
english: Struck by Rāma's arrow, the demon then cried out in Rāma's own voice, screaming in a tone of anguish: "Ah, Sītā! Lakṣmaṇa!"

sanskrit: śuśrāva tasya vaidehī tatas tāṃ karuṇāṃ giram sā prādravad yataḥ śabdas tām uvācātha lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: The daughter of Videha heard that pitiful cry and rushed toward the sound; but Lakṣmaṇa spoke to her.

sanskrit: alaṃ te śaṅkayā bhīru ko rāmaṃ viṣahiṣyati muhūrtād drakṣyase rāmam āgataṃ taṃ śucismite
english: "Fear not, timid one — who could overpower Rāma? Within a moment you shall see him return, O bright-smiling one."

sanskrit: ity uktvā sā prarudatī paryaśaṅkata devaram hatā vai strīsvabhāvena śuddhacāritrabhūṣaṇam
english: Though he spoke thus, she burst into tears and harboured suspicion of her brother-in-law — she was overcome by the nature of women, she whose ornament was her pure character.

sanskrit: sā taṃ paruṣam ārabdhā vaktuṃ sādhvī pativratā naiṣa kālo bhaven mūḍha yaṃ tvaṃ prārthayase hṛdā
english: The chaste and devoted wife began to speak harshly to him: "Fool, the time you are craving in your heart has not come."

sanskrit: apy ahaṃ śastram ādāya hanyām ātmānam ātmanā pateyaṃ giriśṛṅgād vā viśeyaṃ vā hutāśanam
english: "I would take a weapon and kill myself, or leap from a mountain peak, or enter a blazing fire —

sanskrit: rāmaṃ bhartāram utsṛjya na tv ahaṃ tvāṃ kathaṃ cana nihīnam upatiṣṭheyaṃ śārdūlī kroṣṭukaṃ yathā
english: — rather than, abandoning Rāma my husband, ever submit to you, a base creature — as a tigress would not stoop to a jackal."

sanskrit: etādṛśaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā lakṣmaṇaḥ priyarāghavaḥ pidhāya karṇau sadvṛttaḥ prasthito yena rāghavaḥ sa rāmasya padaṃ gṛhya prasasāra dhanurdharaḥ
english: Hearing such words, Lakṣmaṇa — who loved Rāma and was of righteous conduct — covered his ears and set out in the direction Rāma had gone; the bowman followed in Rāma's very footsteps.

sanskrit: etasminn antare rakṣo rāvaṇaḥ pratyadṛśyata abhavyo bhavyarūpeṇa bhasmacchanna ivānalaḥ yativeṣapraticchanno jihīrṣus tām aninditām
english: At that very moment the demon Rāvaṇa appeared — inauspicious though wearing an auspicious disguise, like fire concealed under ashes — dressed as an ascetic mendicant, intent on carrying off the blameless woman.

sanskrit: sā tam ālakṣya saṃprāptaṃ dharmajñā janakātmajā nimantrayām āsa tadā phalamūlāśanādibhiḥ
english: The daughter of Janaka, knowing the duties of dharma, perceived him arriving and received him with an offering of fruits, roots, and other forest food.

sanskrit: avamanya sa tat sarvaṃ svarūpaṃ pratipadya ca sāntvayām āsa vaidehīm iti rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ
english: Scorning all of that, the foremost of demons resumed his true form and set about winning Vaidehī over with soft words.

sanskrit: sīte rākṣasarājo 'haṃ rāvaṇo nāma viśrutaḥ mama laṅkā purī nāmnā ramyā pāre mahodadheḥ
english: "Sītā, I am the celebrated king of the demons, Rāvaṇa by name; my city, Laṅkā by name, lies beautiful on the far shore of the great ocean."

sanskrit: tatra tvaṃ varanārīṣu śobhiṣyasi mayā saha bhāryā me bhava suśroṇi tāpasaṃ tyaja rāghavam
english: "There among the finest women you shall shine at my side. Become my wife, O lovely-hipped one; abandon the ascetic Rāghava."

sanskrit: evamādīni vākyāni śrutvā sītātha jānakī pidhāya karṇau suśroṇī maivam ity abravīd vacaḥ
english: Having heard these and similar words, Sītā, daughter of Janaka, covered her ears and spoke in reply: "It shall not be so."

sanskrit: prapated dyauḥ sanakṣatrā pṛthivī śakalībhavet śaityam agnir iyān nāhaṃ tyajeyaṃ raghunandanam
english: "Let the sky with all its stars fall; let the earth shatter into fragments; let fire turn cold — I will not abandon the son of Raghu."

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi bhinnakaraṭaṃ padminaṃ vanagocaram upasthāya mahānāgaṃ kareṇuḥ sūkaraṃ spṛśet
english: "How could a female elephant, having served the great tusker — its ichor streaming, lotus-decked, ranging the forest — stoop to touch a boar?"

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi pītvā mādhvīkaṃ pītvā ca madhumādhavīm lobhaṃ sauvīrake kuryān nārī kā cid iti smare
english: "How could any woman, having drunk the madhvīka wine and sweet spring honey, ever desire the crude sour gruel — so I hold in my heart."

sanskrit: iti sā taṃ samābhāṣya praviveśāśramaṃ punaḥ tām anudrutya suśroṇīṃ rāvaṇaḥ pratyaṣedhayat
english: Having spoken thus to him, she turned and re-entered the hermitage; Rāvaṇa rushed after the fair-hipped woman and blocked her way.

sanskrit: bhartsayitvā tu rūkṣeṇa svareṇa gatacetanām mūrdhajeṣu nijagrāha kham upācakrame tataḥ
english: Having terrified her senseless with a harsh voice, he seized her by the hair and then ascended into the sky.

sanskrit: tāṃ dadarśa tadā gṛdhro jaṭāyur girigocaraḥ rudatīṃ rāma rāmeti hriyamāṇāṃ tapasvinīm
english: Then the vulture Jaṭāyu, who ranged the mountain heights, saw the wretched woman being carried off weeping, "Rāma! Rāma!"

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca sakhā daśarathasyāsīj jaṭāyur aruṇātmajaḥ gṛdhrarājo mahāvīryaḥ saṃpātir yasya sodaraḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Jaṭāyu, son of Aruṇa, was a dear friend of Daśaratha — the great and mighty king of vultures, whose full brother was Saṃpāti.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa tadā sītāṃ rāvaṇāṅkagatāṃ snuṣām krodhād abhyadravat pakṣī rāvaṇaṃ rākṣaseśvaram
english: He saw Sītā, his friend's daughter-in-law, clasped in Rāvaṇa's arms; filled with rage, the bird flew at Rāvaṇa, lord of the demons.

sanskrit: athainam abravīd gṛdhro muñca muñceti maithilīm dhriyamāṇe mayi kathaṃ hariṣyasi niśācara na hi me mokṣyase jīvan yadi notsṛjase vadhūm
english: The vulture cried out to him: "Release her, release the Maithilī! Night-wanderer, while I yet live how will you carry her away? You shall not escape me alive if you do not let this woman go."

sanskrit: uktvaivaṃ rākṣasendraṃ taṃ cakarta nakharair bhṛśam pakṣatuṇḍaprahāraiś ca bahuśo jarjarīkṛtaḥ cakṣāra rudhiraṃ bhūri giriḥ prasravaṇair iva
english: Having spoken thus to the lord of demons, he tore into him fiercely with his talons; again and again rent by blows of wings and beak, Rāvaṇa poured forth rivers of blood like a mountain streaming waterfalls.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamāno gṛdhreṇa rāmapriyahitaiṣiṇā khaḍgam ādāya ciccheda bhujau tasya patatriṇaḥ
english: Being mauled by the vulture who sought the good of Rāma's beloved, Rāvaṇa drew his sword and cut off both wings of the bird.

sanskrit: nihatya gṛdhrarājaṃ sa chinnābhraśikharopamam ūrdhvam ācakrame sītāṃ gṛhītvāṅkena rākṣasaḥ
english: Having struck down the king of vultures — who now resembled a peak of a severed cloud — the demon took Sītā in his arms and soared upward into the sky.

sanskrit: yatra yatra tu vaidehī paśyaty āśramamaṇḍalam saro vā saritaṃ vāpi tatra muñcati bhūṣaṇam
english: Wherever Vaidehī caught sight of a hermitage settlement, a lake, or a river, she dropped one of her ornaments there.

sanskrit: sā dadarśa giriprasthe pañca vānarapuṃgavān tatra vāso mahad divyam utsasarja manasvinī
english: She saw five great monkeys on a mountain slope; there the spirited woman cast down her large and splendid garment.

sanskrit: tat teṣāṃ vānarendrāṇāṃ papāta pavanoddhutam madhye supītaṃ pañcānāṃ vidyun meghāntare yathā
english: Borne aloft by the wind, it fell among those five monkey lords — brilliant yellow amid them like lightning flashing between clouds.

sanskrit: evaṃ hṛtāyāṃ vaidehyāṃ rāmo hatvā mahāmṛgam nivṛtto dadṛśe dhīmān bhrātaraṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ tadā
english: While Vaidehī was thus being abducted, the wise Rāma, having slain the great deer, turned back and came upon his brother Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: katham utsṛjya vaidehīṃ vane rākṣasasevite ity evaṃ bhrātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā prāpto 'sīti vyagarhayat
english: Seeing his brother coming, he reproved him: "How have you abandoned Vaidehī in a forest frequented by demons and come here?"

sanskrit: mṛgarūpadhareṇātha rakṣasā so 'pakarṣaṇam bhrātur āgamanaṃ caiva cintayan paryatapyata
english: Thinking over the demon's luring him away in the form of a deer, and now his brother's arrival, he burned with anguish.

sanskrit: garhayann eva rāmas tu tvaritas taṃ samāsadat api jīvati vaidehī neti paśyāmi lakṣmaṇa
english: Even as he reproached him, Rāma hurried back to the hermitage. He said: "Lakṣmaṇa, I cannot see whether Vaidehī still lives."

sanskrit: tasya tat sarvam ācakhyau sītāyā lakṣmaṇo vacaḥ yad uktavaty asadṛśaṃ vaidehī paścimaṃ vacaḥ
english: Lakṣmaṇa related to him all of Sītā's words — the unworthy last speech that Vaidehī had spoken.

sanskrit: dahyamānena tu hṛdā rāmo 'bhyapatad āśramam sa dadarśa tadā gṛdhraṃ nihataṃ parvatopamam
english: With his heart burning, Rāma rushed to the hermitage; there he saw the vulture lying slain, huge as a mountain.

sanskrit: rākṣasaṃ śaṅkamānas tu vikṛṣya balavad dhanuḥ abhyadhāvata kākutsthas tatas taṃ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
english: Suspecting a demon, the scion of Kakutstha drew his powerful bow and charged at it, together with Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: sa tāv uvāca tejasvī sahitau rāmalakṣmaṇau gṛdhrarājo 'smi bhadraṃ vāṃ sakhā daśarathasya ha
english: The radiant bird spoke to both Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa as they stood together: "I am the king of vultures; blessings on you — I was a friend of Daśaratha."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā saṃgṛhya dhanuṣī śubhe ko 'yaṃ pitaram asmākaṃ nāmnāhety ūcatuś ca tau
english: Hearing those words, both drew back their fine bows and said: "Who are you, who speaks our father by name?"

sanskrit: tato dadṛśatus tau taṃ chinnapakṣadvayaṃ tathā tayoḥ śaśaṃsa gṛdhras tu sītārthe rāvaṇād vadham
english: Then they saw him with both wings severed; and the vulture told them how he had been struck down by Rāvaṇa on Sītā's behalf.

sanskrit: apṛcchad rāghavo gṛdhraṃ rāvaṇaḥ kāṃ diśaṃ gataḥ tasya gṛdhraḥ śiraḥkampair ācacakṣe mamāra ca
english: Rāghava asked the vulture: "In which direction did Rāvaṇa go?" The vulture indicated it by nodding his head — and then he died.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇām iti kākutstho viditvāsya tad iṅgitam saṃskāraṃ lambhayām āsa sakhāyaṃ pūjayan pituḥ
english: Understanding from his gesture that the direction was south, the scion of Kakutstha performed the funeral rites, honouring him as a friend of his father.

sanskrit: tato dṛṣṭvāśramapadaṃ vyapaviddhabṛsīghaṭam vidhvastakalaśaṃ śūnyaṃ gomāyubalasevitam
english: Then, seeing the hermitage site — cushions and water-pots scattered, the sacred jars overturned, deserted, prowled by packs of jackals —

sanskrit: duḥkhaśokasamāviṣṭau vaidehīharaṇārditau jagmatur daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ dakṣiṇena paraṃtapau
english: — both overwhelmed with grief and anguish, tormented by Vaidehī's abduction, the two scorchers of foes entered the Daṇḍaka forest heading southward.

sanskrit: vane mahati tasmiṃs tu rāmaḥ saumitriṇā saha dadarśa mṛgayūthāni dravamāṇāni sarvaśaḥ śabdaṃ ca ghoraṃ sattvānāṃ dāvāgner iva vardhataḥ
english: In that great forest, Rāma together with the son of Sumitrā saw herds of deer fleeing in all directions and heard a dreadful roar of creatures swelling like a forest fire.

sanskrit: apaśyetāṃ muhūrtāc ca kabandhaṃ ghoradarśanam meghaparvatasaṃkāśaṃ śālaskandhaṃ mahābhujam urogataviśālākṣaṃ mahodaramahāmukham
english: And shortly they saw Kabandha — dreadful to behold — resembling a cloud-mountain, massive as a śāla trunk, with enormous arms, wide eyes set in his chest, a vast belly, and an enormous mouth.

sanskrit: yadṛcchayātha tad rakṣaḥ kare jagrāha lakṣmaṇam viṣādam agamat sadyaḥ saumitrir atha bhārata
english: Then, O Bhārata, that demon seized Lakṣmaṇa in his hand at random; Saumitri was instantly seized with despair.

sanskrit: sa rāmam abhisaṃprekṣya kṛṣyate yena tanmukham viṣaṇṇaś cābravīd rāmaṃ paśyāvasthām imāṃ mama
english: Looking toward Rāma as he was being dragged — his face turned that way — he said despondently to Rāma: "See the plight I am in."

sanskrit: haraṇaṃ caiva vaidehyā mama cāyam upaplavaḥ rājyabhraṃśaś ca bhavatas tātasya maraṇaṃ tathā
english: "The abduction of Vaidehī, and now this calamity of mine — your loss of the kingdom, and the death of our father as well —

sanskrit: nāhaṃ tvāṃ saha vaidehyā sametaṃ kosalāgatam drakṣyāmi pṛthivīrājye pitṛpaitāmahe sthitam
english: "— I shall not see you arrived in Kosala together with Vaidehī, established in the ancestral kingdom of your fathers."

sanskrit: drakṣyanty āryasya dhanyā ye kuśalājaśamīlavaiḥ abhiṣiktasya vadanaṃ somaṃ sābhralavaṃ yathā
english: "Fortunate are those who will see the noble one's face after his coronation — like the moon glimmering through rifts in a cloud — adorned with kuśa grass, aja, and śamī branches."

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ dhīmān vilalāpa sa lakṣmaṇaḥ tam uvācātha kākutsthaḥ saṃbhrameṣv apy asaṃbhramaḥ
english: Thus in many ways did the wise Lakṣmaṇa lament; and Kākutstha, who kept composure even in crises, spoke to him.

sanskrit: mā viṣīda naravyāghra naiṣa kaś cin mayi sthite chindhy asya dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ chinnaḥ savyo mayā bhujaḥ
english: "Do not despair, tiger among men — while I stand here, this creature is nothing. Cut off his right arm; I have already severed the left."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ vadatā tasya bhujo rāmeṇa pātitaḥ khaḍgena bhṛśatīkṣṇena nikṛttas tilakāṇḍavat
english: Even as he spoke these words, Rāma's exceedingly sharp sword sliced off the arm — cut clean as a stalk of sesame.

sanskrit: tato 'sya dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ khaḍgenājaghnivān balī saumitrir api saṃprekṣya bhrātaraṃ rāghavaṃ sthitam
english: Then the mighty Saumitri too, glancing at his brother Rāghava standing firm, hewed off the demon's right arm with his sword.

sanskrit: punar abhyāhanat pārśve tad rakṣo lakṣmaṇo bhṛśam gatāsur apatad bhūmau kabandhaḥ sumahāṃs tataḥ
english: Lakṣmaṇa struck that demon hard in the flank again, and then the immense Kabandha fell lifeless to the ground.

sanskrit: tasya dehād viniḥsṛtya puruṣo divyadarśanaḥ dadṛśe divam āsthāya divi sūrya iva jvalan
english: From his body there emerged a being of divine appearance, who was seen rising to the sky and blazing there like the sun.

sanskrit: papraccha rāmas taṃ vāgmī kas tvaṃ prabrūhi pṛcchataḥ kāmayā kim idaṃ citram āścaryaṃ pratibhāti me
english: The eloquent Rāma asked him: "Who are you? Tell me, I ask. By what cause does this wonderful marvel appear before me?"

sanskrit: tasyācacakṣe gandharvo viśvāvasur ahaṃ nṛpa prāpto brahmānuśāpena yoniṃ rākṣasasevitām
english: The gandharva revealed to him: "O king, I am Viśvāvasu; through a curse of Brahmā I fell into a birth haunted by demons."

sanskrit: rāvaṇena hṛtā sītā rājñā laṅkānivāsinā sugrīvam abhigacchasva sa te sāhyaṃ kariṣyati
english: "Sītā has been abducted by the king Rāvaṇa, who dwells in Laṅkā. Seek out Sugrīva — he will render you aid."

sanskrit: eṣā pampā śivajalā haṃsakāraṇḍavāyutā ṛśyamūkasya śailasya saṃnikarṣe taṭākinī
english: "Here is the Pampā lake — its waters auspicious, full of geese and karaṇḍava ducks — a lovely tarn close to the mountain Ṛśyamūka."

sanskrit: saṃvasaty atra sugrīvaś caturbhiḥ sacivaiḥ saha bhrātā vānararājasya vālino hemamālinaḥ
english: "Sugrīva dwells here with four ministers — the brother of Vālin, the golden-garlanded king of the monkeys."

sanskrit: etāvac chakyam asmābhir vaktuṃ draṣṭāsi jānakīm dhruvaṃ vānararājasya vidito rāvaṇālayaḥ
english: "This much is within my power to tell you: you will see Jānakī. The abode of Rāvaṇa is certainly known to the king of monkeys."

sanskrit: ity uktvāntarhito divyaḥ puruṣaḥ sa mahāprabhaḥ vismayaṃ jagmatuś cobhau tau vīrau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: Having spoken thus, that divine being of great radiance disappeared; and both those heroes, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, were filled with wonder.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tato 'vidūre nalinīṃ prabhūtakamalotpalām sītāharaṇaduḥkhārtaḥ pampāṃ rāmaḥ samāsadat
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then, not far off, Rāma — his heart aching over Sītā's abduction — came to Pampā, a pond full of abundant lotuses and blue water-lilies.

sanskrit: mārutena suśītena sukhenāmṛtagandhinā sevyamāno vane tasmiñ jagāma manasā priyām
english: Fanned by a cool and gentle breeze fragrant as nectar, he wandered through that forest, going in his mind to his beloved.

sanskrit: vilalāpa sa rājendras tatra kāntām anusmaran kāmabāṇābhisaṃtaptaḥ saumitris tam athābravīt
english: That lord among kings lamented there, calling his beloved to mind, scorched by the arrows of love; and Saumitri then spoke to him.

sanskrit: na tvām evaṃvidho bhāvaḥ spraṣṭum arhati mānada ita ātmavantam iva vyādhiḥ puruṣaṃ vṛddhaśīlinam
english: "Such a state of feeling does not befit you, O giver of honour — no more than illness befits a self-possessed man of mature virtue."

sanskrit: pravṛttir upalabdhā te vaidehyā rāvaṇasya ca tāṃ tvaṃ puruṣakāreṇa buddhyā caivopapādaya
english: "You have obtained tidings of Vaidehī and of Rāvaṇa; pursue that now through manly effort and through reason."

sanskrit: abhigacchāva sugrīvaṃ śailasthaṃ haripuṃgavam mayi śiṣye ca bhṛtye ca sahāye ca samāśvasa
english: "Let us approach Sugrīva, that foremost of monkeys dwelling on the mountain. Take heart — in me you have a disciple, a servant, and an ally."

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhair vākyair lakṣmaṇena sa rāghavaḥ uktaḥ prakṛtim āpede kārye cānantaro 'bhavat
english: Thus addressed by Lakṣmaṇa with many such words, that son of Raghu regained his composure and became single-minded in the task at hand.

sanskrit: niṣevya vāri pampāyās tarpayitvā pitṝn api pratasthatur ubhau vīrau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: Having drunk from the waters of Pampā and poured libations to their ancestors, both hero brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, set forth.

sanskrit: tāv ṛśyamūkam abhyetya bahumūlaphalaṃ girim giryagre vānarān pañca vīrau dadṛśatus tadā
english: Approaching Ṛśyamūka — the mountain rich in roots and fruits — the two heroes saw five monkeys on the mountain's summit.

sanskrit: sugrīvaḥ preṣayām āsa sacivaṃ vānaraṃ tayoḥ buddhimantaṃ hanūmantaṃ himavantam iva sthitam
english: Sugrīva dispatched to them his minister, the monkey Hanūmān — steady as the Himālaya and possessed of great wisdom.

sanskrit: tena saṃbhāṣya pūrvaṃ tau sugrīvam abhijagmatuḥ sakhyaṃ vānararājena cakre rāmas tato nṛpa
english: After first conversing with him, the two went to Sugrīva; and then, O king, Rāma formed a bond of friendship with the king of monkeys.

sanskrit: tad vāso darśayām āsus tasya kārye nivedite vānarāṇāṃ tu yat sītā hriyamāṇābhyavāsṛjat
english: When his need was made known, the monkeys showed him that garment which Sītā, as she was being carried away, had cast down upon them.

sanskrit: tat pratyayakaraṃ labdhvā sugrīvaṃ plavagādhipam pṛthivyāṃ vānaraiśvarye svayaṃ rāmo 'bhyaṣecayat
english: Having received that proof, Rāma himself consecrated Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, to sovereignty over all the monkeys of the earth.
